note: Added 2026-09-09 together with 13 sibling Greater Vancouver property tax notices, on request, to grow `propertytax` coverage from 6 documents to 20. Not a municipal tax notice at all: a UBC Services Levy invoice billed by the university for the difference between the City of Vancouver and Provincial Rural Area tax rates. It is nonetheless classified propertytax, which is the intended reading. THIS DOCUMENT IS THE ANCHOR FOR THE LEADING-'THE' VENDOR NORMALISATION: the letterhead prints 'THE UNIVERSITY OF BRITISH COLUMBIA' (extract twin) while the generate twin returns the registry spelling 'University of British Columbia'. Before _normalize_vendor dropped a leading 'the' the two token lists differed, no structural branch of _prefer_vendor_generate matched, and the confidence tiebreak decided -- measured a 50/50 coin flip across 12 live reads (6 each) on a base-critical field that auto-writes. invoice_number 'CI-0000273375' is a REAL read from the printed 'Invoice Number' label, not the filename fallback the other tax notices rely on. total 1,837.44 from 'Total Payment Outstanding'; the outstanding-balance and interest lines both print $0.00, so nothing is carried forward. invoice_date IS asserted: 'Invoice Date: Jul 8, 2026' is printed. payment_due_date from 'Due Date 2026-08-07'. account_number is the printed Roll Number 01060018. Table A on this page prints 'City of Vancouver' four times as a RATE COMPARISON rather than as the biller -- measured: CU never once chose it as the vendor across 12 reads. || invoice_description NOT asserted: free-text that rewords itself every run. || The narrative fields (diagnosis_solution, recommendation, warranty and their zh_hant twins) are blank by policy on a municipal bill. || folio_number ADDED 2026-09-09 with the new folio twins (commercial-narrative-v20). It is a critical field on property tax notices only (field_policy.PROPERTYTAX_DELTA), and is asserted on every sidecar -- the value on a tax notice, "" everywhere else -- so a regression that starts populating it on ordinary invoices is caught. || number_of_days ASSERTION REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 property_* sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume number_of_days for property tax. It was removed from the whole family rather than only where it flakes, so the tax notices stay uniform. Behaviour seen: the period resolves 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 on every read (365 days inclusive), number_of_days_extract returns no value at all, and number_of_days_generate intermittently invents '1' -- catalogued defect B3 -- which reconcile_number_of_days then corrects to 365, while an empty twin pair stays blank by that function's explicit 'corrects only; never supplies' design. The field therefore flipped '' <-> 365 between runs. || billing_period_start_date AND billing_period_end_date ASSERTIONS REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 propertytax sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume the billing period for property tax, so the corpus no longer asserts it on this family. Both fields REMAIN in WRITE_FIELDS and still reach Dynamics -- removing the assertion stops the corpus checking them, it does not stop them being written. What this gives up, stated once: on the 16 notices that asserted '' the pair was the guard against a generate twin inventing a period out of nothing, and on property_surrey it was catching a real failure chain -- B3's invented number_of_days=1 makes the code derive start = end - 1 day, which collapses the period to zero length and blanks a correct 2026-01-01 (open-defects A13b, measured 4 of 6 reads correct). That chain is unfixed and is now invisible to the corpus on every property tax notice. || account_number is written WITHOUT the 'Account No: ' prefix on this family (user requirement, 2026-09-09, propertytax ONLY -- every other municipal bill and every commercial invoice keeps the label). The written value is the bare folio, which is what an owner quotes to the municipality.
